title: Cannot type the first character with accent in the search field of Kickoff due to search field not being focused by default
line: Accented letters typed with a compose key, dead key or input method right after opening Kickoff now keep their accent.
explanation: Kickoff opened with keyboard focus on the favorites grid and only forwarded the typed key events to the search field. Qt's compose handling and input methods only process keys when a text field has focus, so the compose/dead key was dropped and the bare letter landed in the field ("e'" instead of "é"). The search field now takes focus when Kickoff opens; while it holds that opening focus, keys are first forwarded through the same items the focused grid would have passed them to, so arrows, Tab, Enter, Menu, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown behave exactly as before until the user types or moves focus.

commits.message:
applets/kickoff: focus the search field when opening

Compose keys and input methods only work in a focused text field, so the
first accented letter typed after opening Kickoff lost its accent. The
field now gets focus, while arrows, Tab and Enter still act on the menu.

BUG: 459269

media.caption: Compose key: open Kickoff with Meta, then Compose, e, ' gives "e'"
Same keys with the fix give "é"

review.text: Focusing the search field on open is the right fix: compose keys and input methods only work in a focused text field. The 'focusedOnOpen' mode correctly keeps navigation as on master, which answers the objection that closed !3252. The way it does that is fragile, though: Keys.forwardTo rebuilds Qt Quick's focus chain by walking parents from the current item up to root.parent, and a dummy Item catches Up. Any change to Kickoff's item tree or key handlers would silently break it. Maintainers are unlikely to take that over a simpler, explicit version.
changes: Drop the parent-chain walk and the dummy upFromContentHandler item. While focusedOnOpen, forward only to the existing targets (the view, or the inner grid view for ListOfGridsView) with Keys.BeforeItem.

Handle keys that need the delegate (Enter/Return, Menu) explicitly, by calling the current item's action or context menu. Alternatively, on the first non-text navigation key hand focus to kickoff.contentArea and forward that one key, so the menu goes back to master's focus state instead of emulating it.
